title: Equivariant fan regularization with projectivity and relative smooth charts
statement: Let $F$ be a field and $X$ an integral finite-type $F$-scheme [def-weil-field, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $B\subset X$ be closed with dense complement $U$ such that its divisorial log scheme $(X,M)$ is fine saturated and log regular [def-trf-log-regular-pair, def-trf-fs-log-blowup] with triviality locus exactly $U$ (thus $(X,B)$ is a log regular pair), and is log smooth over the trivial log field $(\operatorname{Spec}F,F^\times)$ [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Let a finite group $J$ act compatibly on $X,F$, preserving $B$; the action on $F$ need not be trivial. There exists a finite $J$-equivariant tower $(X_n,M_n)\to\cdots\to(X_0,M_0)=(X,M)$ of saturated log blowups along nonempty coherent log ideals. Its contracted pullback to any strict etale fan-chart neighbourhood agrees with the pullback of a saturated smooth-functorial fan desingularization; these identifications preserve the ordered centers and respect composition and finite disjoint unions [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup, def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. The action on the tower respects the group law. Each underlying stage is the normalization in the common function field of the ordinary blowup of the preceding scheme along the nonzero finite-type ideal generated by its log center [def-sc-normalization, def-nagata-global-blowup]. Every normalization map is finite; all stages are integral Noetherian finite-type $F$-schemes, and the composite $a:X_n\to X$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense and birational [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. It is an isomorphism over $U$. Every stage is log regular and log smooth over the trivial log field, with triviality locus the inverse image of $U$. Every final characteristic monoid is a free monoid $\mathbf N^r$, $r\geq0$. In particular $X_n$ is regular and smooth over $F$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For $B_n=(a^{-1}B)_{\mathrm{red}}$, etale locally at each geometric point there is a smooth $F$-map to $\mathbf A^r_F$ for which $B_n$ is the inverse image of $V(z_1\cdots z_r)$ and its divisorial log chart is $\mathbf N^r$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. The chart can be chosen with all $r$ coordinate branches passing through the chosen point. Each intersection of local branches is smooth over $F$ of the expected codimension. No separatedness or perfection hypothesis is imposed; global boundary components may self-intersect. A length-zero tower and empty boundary are allowed. Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth].

source.place: VIII 3.3.13--3.3.15 and 3.4.4--3.4.9, pp.108--112, and 4.1.1 p.117; X Lemma 2.2 p.149 smooth-pair-over-a-field refinement. Returned steps 7--9: strict fan descent, normalized blowup projectivity, and free-characteristic relative charts.

proof.text: The field spectrum is Noetherian: its sole local ring is the field and its space has one point. Thus $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. At each geometric point the characteristic $P$ is fs sharp by [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart]. Apply [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] to $Q=P$ and its zero face: $P^{\rm gp}$ is free abelian of finite rank, in particular torsion free. Fix the saturated smooth-functorial fan resolution $\mathcal R$ of [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization]. The finite strict etale fan-chart cover required below exists by [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](i).

source.place: VIII 3.2.20--3.2.21 and 3.3.15, pp.106,109; VI 1.6, p.70; Noetherian and quasi-separated input: Stacks 01T6 and 01OY.

proof.text: Let $(V,N)$ be a quasi-compact locally Noetherian fs log scheme with torsion-free characteristic group completions and a global fan chart $c:(V,\overline N)\to H$ to a fine fan. First make $H$ admissible for $\mathcal R$. Each $v\in V$ has a neighbourhood mapping into the affine localization $H_{c(v)}$; by quasi-compactness finitely many of these cover $V$, so $c$ factors through their union $H'$, an open subfan with a finite affine cover, and $c$ is still a fan chart. The stalk of $H$ at $c(v)$ is $\overline N_v$, the sharp quotient of an fs chart monoid by a face, hence fs by [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening]; the stalk at any other point of $H_{c(v)}$ is, by the affine model in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], the sharpened localization of that fs monoid at a face, whose group completion is free by [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening]. Thus $H'$ is torsion free and $\mathcal R(H')$ is defined; by the open-localization compatibility of [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization] the choice of the finite subcover changes it only by canonical contracted identifications. Recursively pull back the finite fan tower $\mathcal R(H')$ using [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii). At level $i$ with fan center $K_i$, the center is the inverse image in $N_i$ of the ideal generated by $c_i^{-1}K_i$ in $\overline N_i$. The cited result constructs the next saturated log blowup, its fan chart, and its characteristic-stalk identification. Each center is nonempty coherent. Delete exactly those stages whose center is the whole log monoid sheaf. Such a center is already invertible, so the identity satisfies the universal property of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] and is canonically its blowup. Call the contracted ordered tower $\mathcal T_c(V,N)$.

For a strict morphism between two globally charted inputs, [lem-trf-strict-fan-chart-local-comparison] identifies the two chart maps, near each source point, through an isomorphism of affine fan localizations. The open-localization and isomorphism compatibilities of [lem-trf-functorial-fan-desingularization] identify the contracted restrictions of their fan towers, with the same ordered centers. Their inverse-image log ideals are consequently equal; [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii) identifies the corresponding log towers. These comparisons are canonical: with the center and previous stage fixed, the universal property of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] uniquely identifies the next stage over its base. Therefore local comparisons agree on overlaps and respect identity and composition. Taking the strict map to be the identity proves chart independence. Taking it strict etale gives the contracted strict etale pullback comparisons. The fan rule's finite-disjoint-union compatibility gives the same comparisons for the component inclusions. Thus the rule on globally charted inputs satisfies all hypotheses of [lem-trf-functorial-log-blowup-etale-descent].

source.place: VIII proof of 3.3.15, pp.109--110, local fan comparison, finite-disjoint-union argument and descent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-functorial-log-blowup-etale-descent] to get a finite tower $\mathcal T(X,M)$ on $X$ with nonempty coherent log ideals and all the specified comparisons on strict etale fan-chart neighborhoods. The comparisons preserve the centers and their order, and satisfy composition and finite-disjoint-union compatibility, as verified before descent. On a chart cover its terminal characteristic stalks identify, by [lem-trf-log-fan-chart-blowup](ii), with stalks of the smooth terminal fan of $\mathcal R$; these are $\mathbf N^r$ by [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Contracted identity stages do not change the last log scheme. Strict etale pullback preserves characteristic stalks and gives etale covers on underlying schemes; the latter covers remain jointly surjective at every stage by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]. Hence every terminal geometric characteristic on $X_n$ is free, including rank zero.

source.place: VIII Theorem 3.3.15 and its proof, pp.109--110; strict etale cover base change: Stacks 02GO and 01S1.

proof.text: Since each $g\in J$ preserves $B$ and $U$, its pullback on regular functions carries functions invertible on $U$ to functions invertible on $U$. The formula for the divisorial log structure in [def-trf-log-regular-pair] therefore makes $g$ a strict log automorphism of $(X,M)$. Use the canonical strict-isomorphism comparison of the descended procedure to lift $g$ to its tower. There is no change of length under an isomorphism: a pulled-back center is the whole monoid exactly when the original center is. The identity and composition laws proved above imply $\widetilde{1}=1$ and $\widetilde{gh}=\widetilde g\widetilde h$, on every stage and its center. Thus this is a $J$-equivariant tower. This construction concerns log automorphisms, not automorphisms over $F$, so it applies to the given semilinear action on $X$ and $F$ without requiring that $J$ fix $F$.

source.place: VIII 3.3.15 and 3.4.9, pp.109--112, functoriality restricted to automorphisms; divisorial action as in VI 1.4, p.69.

proof.text: Induct on the levels, beginning with integral finite-type log regular $X_0=X$. Suppose these properties and the prescribed triviality locus hold for $X_i$. By [lem-trf-log-blowup-normalization], its next saturated log blowup is log regular, has triviality locus exactly the inverse image of the preceding one, and its underlying map is $(\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}X_i)^\nu\to\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}X_i\to X_i$, where $J_i$ is the nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent ideal generated by the log center. Put $Z_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}X_i$. By [lem-sfb-integral-blowup-projective-geometry], $Z_i$ is integral and $Z_i\to X_i$ is projective in the bundle sense; it is proper and hence finite type by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper] and [def-weil-proper-morphism]. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $Z_i$ is finite type over $F$, so [lem-sc-normalization-exists] applies: $\nu_i:X_{i+1}\to Z_i$ is finite, surjective and birational. By the definition of normalization [def-sc-normalization], its affine rings are integral closures inside $F(X_i)$, hence domains, and its generic field is $F(X_i)$. Thus $X_{i+1}$ is integral with the same function field.

source.place: VIII 3.4.5--3.4.9, pp.111--112; ordinary blowup: Stacks 02ND,02NS; normalization finiteness: Stacks 035S as used in lem-sc-normalization-exists.

proof.text: The finite morphism $\nu_i$ is projective in the bundle sense by [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle]. Since $X_i$ is Noetherian and thus qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], compose $\nu_i$ with $Z_i\to X_i$ using [lem-sfb-projective-bundle-composition]. The step $X_{i+1}\to X_i$ is therefore projective, hence proper and finite type by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper] and [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], so $X_{i+1}$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. This closes the induction in the preceding step. Repeated projective-bundle composition over the fixed qcqs target $X$ gives projectivity of $a:X_n\to X$ in exactly the convention stated, with no separatedness assumption on $X/F$. For length zero the identity embeds in $\mathbf P_X(\mathcal O_X)=X$, so the same conclusion holds.

source.place: VIII 3.4.8--3.4.9; Stacks 0B3I finite projectivity, 0C4P bundle-projective composition, 01OY quasi-separatedness and 01T6 finite-type Noetherian schemes.

proof.text: At each level [lem-trf-log-blowup-normalization] identifies the map over the preceding triviality locus with an isomorphism and identifies the new triviality locus with its full inverse image. Starting from the explicit hypothesis that the initial triviality locus is $U$, induction gives $U_i=a_i^{-1}U\simeq U$ at every stage, where $a_i:X_i\to X$ is the composite. The normalization comparison also gives the same function field at every level, as computed above. The nonempty open $U_i$ is dense in integral $X_i$; thus $a$ is an isomorphism between dense opens and is birational. This proves both the asserted unchanged-open clause and the common-function-field interpretation of all normalizations.

source.place: VIII 3.4.1,3.4.5--3.4.9, pp.110--112; dense-open argument for integral schemes.

proof.text: Every saturated log blowup is log etale by [lem-sfb-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change]. Its composition with the preceding log-smooth structure map to the trivial log field is log smooth by the same node. Induction from the assumed log smoothness of $X$ therefore gives log smoothness over $F$ at every stage. The log regularity at each stage was already supplied by the normalization comparison, not inferred from ordinary regularity or from perfection of $F$.

By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure], $M_n$ is the divisorial log structure of its triviality locus $U_n=a^{-1}U$. Its complementary reduced closed subscheme is precisely $B_n=(a^{-1}B)_{\mathrm{red}}$. The final log structure is fs and log smooth, $X_n$ is finite type over $F$, and all geometric characteristics are free by the chart construction. These are exactly condition (a) of [lem-sfb-free-characteristic-relative-nc-criterion]. Condition (b) supplies at every geometric point the smooth $F$-map to $\mathbf A_F^r$, the boundary equation $z_1\cdots z_r=0$, and its divisorial $\mathbf N^r$ chart, with all coordinate branches through the point. That node also gives smoothness of $X_n/F$ and smooth branch intersections of the expected codimension. Finally [lem-trf-free-characteristic-regular-boundary] applies to the log regular $X_n$ with free characteristics and gives regularity of its ordinary local rings. These are local branches; no assertion of global strictness is needed, so global self-intersections are allowed. Empty boundary gives $r=0$ and the empty coordinate product is $1$.

source.place: VI 1.4--1.7, pp.69--70; VIII 3.4.4, p.110; X Proposition 1.2, pp.136--139, trivial group and trivial base log structure; X Lemma 2.2 proof, p.149, relative smooth-pair interpretation.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q100-f7d14cef4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full item and the statement of every cited node; there are no new nodes. I checked the sources at ILO VIII 3.3.15 and its proof (pp.109-110), VIII 3.4.6-3.4.9 (pp.111-112), VI 1.4-1.7 and X 1.2/2.2 (through the relative-NC criterion), and the Stacks tags. No SGA source is used. The statement change 'triviality locus exactly U' is correct: for X=A^2 and B={0}, Hartogs makes M trivial, so every log blowup is the identity and the boundary conclusion fails. def-trf-log-regular-pair already requires this triviality locus, and both citers (nodal-smooth-pair-resolution and quasi-split-tower-smooth-resolution) supply it through marked-nodal-relative-log-charts. The narrowing is accepted and no target is weakened. Steps 1 and 3-10 apply the cited statements with all hypotheses met: fs-sharp characteristics with free group completions, strict fan-chart comparison to descent as in ILO 3.3.15, the normalized-blowup comparison (VIII 3.4.6), integral-blowup projectivity, normalization finiteness for integral finite-type schemes, qcqs composition of bundle-projective maps with no separatedness, log-etale blowups composed with log-smooth maps, then the divisorial structure and criterion (a)=>(b) plus the regular-boundary lemma. My one repair is to Step 2. The descent rule must be defined on every global fan chart c:V->H, but the fan resolution R is defined only on torsion-free fans with a finite affine cover, and 'admissible input' was never defined. The fix shrinks H to a finite union H' of the affine localizations H_{c(v)} (V is quasi-compact); H' is torsion free by lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening and the affine model of def-trf-fine-fan-blowup, and the open-localization compatibility makes the choice of subcover irrelevant. Both citations are added to Step 2's uses; proof_deps are unchanged. The corrected item file is fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/lem-sfb-equivariant-log-smooth-fan-regularization.json. The edge cases (length zero, empty boundary, non-separated X, imperfect F, self-intersecting components) are handled. I found no duplicates: lem-trf-monoidal-resolution-tower gives existence only, lem-per-gabber-log-blowup-regularization needs X separated, and lem-per-log-regular-projective-log-resolution needs a quasi-projective excellent base. Maintainer note: lem-per-gabber-log-blowup-regularization overlaps this item. Every batch-5 trf citation is general log or projective geometry, outside both assumed statements, and is accepted; the split_report tool_uses are accepted.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
